summary: Track complete managed VM disk chains locally and refuse unsafe chain changes or reuse; API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: There is no new operator workflow; existing power troubleshooting already tells operators to inspect the VM on its host when the host cannot establish a safe state.

api.reason: Existing VM power, edit/delete and storage operations can now fail closed when the host cannot reconcile its managed disk chain. No contract fields, endpoint, capability, or snapshot operation are added; reservation evidence remains internal and has no operation producer yet.

roadmap.reason: The S1 implementation advances the planned host-side chain-safety gate without changing milestone status or scope.

state.record: Nex Core's vmhost managed journal stores ordered disk heads and backing-layer paths; the pool master continues to own VM authority and immutable recovery reservations. A replacement Controller re-adopts VM definitions through the existing Core inventory while chain paths remain host-local.
state.reason: Backing paths are host-specific execution state and must persist with the executing Core; pool authorization bindings remain in the master-owned pool VM record.

verification.method: `go test -race -timeout 20m ./internal/vmhost` passed after the historical-delete ownership guard. Focused regressions cover ordered chain parsing, malformed/truncated/cyclic/deep chains, paused guests selecting live XML, full foreign backing references omitted from partial domain XML, raw foreign disk and CD-ROM handling, external-data/encryption refusal, BUG-0591 where a foreign domain references a disk retained by an earlier successful VM revision, and empty recovery reservations on a fresh host. Existing lifecycle fixtures use a test-only chain observer where they model libvirt without qemu-img.
